Hi Kim (and team),

Thanks for sending the draft. Procurement reviewed and attached a marked-up Order Form (Fontana_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). A few items blocking internal approval: 

- Invoice recipient: we need invoices issued to Fontana Holdings, Inc. (US entity) for all charges. Can Redwood support invoicing to a different legal entity than the contracting entity?
- Tax treatment: our tax team is asking whether Redwood will gross-up charges for withholding when required by local law, or if taxes will be shown as a separate line and borne by Fontana.
- Net terms: fontana prefers Net-45 for this pilot; your draft says Net-30. Is Net-45 acceptable?
- Activation/Proration: we expect first-month proration for activation credits; please confirm how activation fee will be invoiced and whether it can be split across entities.

We'd like to get to signature next week if possible. Can you confirm Redwood's stance on the invoice recipient/payer entity and tax gross-up? Also looping in our PO team (procurement@fontana.io) for PO number flow.

Claire — thanks for the redlines and clear list. Quick responses below and then I'll loop Legal/Finance for definitive language: 

- Invoicing to a different legal entity: we can typically route invoices to a different payor entity if the payor signs a short acknowledgement (billing addendum) and we have W-9/TIN or equivalent. I will confirm with Finance on whether that requires an amendment to the Order Form or an attached billing addendum.
- Tax gross-up vs separate line: Stanford Finance (our tax team) prefers to show taxes separately and have the customer bear taxes unless there's an explicit gross-up in the SOW. Ben — do you have a concise clause we can offer?
- Net-45: I can ask Commercial to approve Net-45 for this pilot; not guaranteed, but likely given size. Jordan — can you run Net-45 through revenue ops and confirm impact?
- Activation proration: we support proration; we usually include a pro forma invoice for the activation month and then standard invoicing thereafter.

I'll attach the order form to Legal for redline review and propose a short billing addendum template if that's necessary. Targeting a reply by EOD Friday.

Best,

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form and tax questions — proposed clause language

Kim / team — reviewed Fontana's redlines. Key legal points and suggested edits below (I attached a redline for insertion):

1) Invoice recipient / payor entity
Suggested language (short addendum):
"Billing Addendum: Redwood will issue invoices to the Payor Entity specified in writing by Customer. Customer must provide valid tax residency documentation and, for U.S. payors, a completed W-9. The Payor Entity acknowledges responsibility for payment of all invoiced amounts regardless of contracting entity relationship."
Rationale: keeps MSA unchanged but creates a simple addendum for operational flexibility.

2) Taxes / gross-up
Suggested clause:
"Taxes: Unless otherwise agreed in writing, amounts set forth in any Order Form are exclusive of taxes. Customer is responsible for all applicable taxes (including withholding taxes) imposed on payments to Redwood. If Customer is required by applicable law to withhold taxes, Customer shall gross-up the payment such that Redwood receives the full amount invoiced, unless Customer provides valid documentary evidence that Redwood is not subject to taxation in the Customer's jurisdiction, in which case the parties shall work in good faith to reflect the correct tax treatment."
Rationale: protects Redwood revenue while allowing documentary carve-outs.

3) Net terms / credit risk
Recommendation: Accept Net-45 for pilot but require upfront PO and first invoice pre-pay or retention clause (e.g., 10% holdback until payment clears) if Finance flags elevated credit risk. Jordan, please confirm operational acceptance.

4) Activation proration & split invoicing
We can support proration. If Fontana requests split invoicing across entities, require a signed intercompany acknowledgement and acceptance of tax risk allocation. Short note to include in billing addendum.

Next steps I propose:
- Kim to send the billing addendum template to Claire and Fontana procurement.
- If Fontana agrees, Legal will incorporate the two short paragraphs above into the Order Form redline and re-send for signoff.

Ben
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Claire — following up with the proposed approach. Attached is a two-part package: 1) a short Billing Addendum template that lets Fontana nominate the payor entity and provide tax docs, and 2) the Order Form with Ben's two-paragraph tax/invoicing insert. Highlights: 

- We can issue invoices to Fontana Holdings, Inc. once you provide the entity name, legal address, and W-9 (or local equivalent).
- Taxes: our standard position is that taxes are separate; we have added the gross-up fallback only where your tax docs indicate Redwood is subject to withholding.
- Net-45: Commercial has provisionally approved Net-45 for the pilot; Finance requests PO prior to first invoice (per Jordan).
- Activation proration: supported; we included a note that activation fees may be invoiced pro forma and netted on the first full invoice.

Please review the two attachments and let us know if Fontana can accept the billing addendum + the inserted language. If yes, we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and target signature by next Wednesday.
